newsitem.title: UK: Abtrust Lloyd's buys Names agency business.
newsitem.headline: Abtrust Lloyd's buys Names agency business.

text.p: Abtrust Lloyd's Insurance Trust Plc (ALIT) said on Tuesday it is to acquire the business of Lloyds of London members' agency Cox Tudberry & Wills Ltd.
"The immediate acquisition cost will not exceed the value of assets acquired being a maximum of 240,000 stg," ALIT said in a statement.
The acquisition of CTW's business -- the management of its 451 Names' Lloyd's interests -- by ALIT follows a court ruling in early February disqualifying three CTW directors as company directors.
The sale of CTW's business had been widely expected in the wake of the court ruling and forms part of Lloyd's market-wide consolidation after record market losses in the early 1990s.
CTW will fulfil its existing agreements with its Names -- the traditional individual backers of the Lloyd's insurance market -- but will not undertake any new business in 1998.
CTW had net assets of some 900,000 stg at end September, but ALIS is acquiring only part of these and CTW will retain the benefit of profit commission arising out of underwriting years up to 1997.
Lloyd's operates a three year accounting system, so results for 1997 will not be announced until 2000.

ALIT will transfer those CTW Names who agree to the move to a new members' agency company, ALIT Insurance Services Ltd (ALIS). CTW's Names have combined capacity in Lloyd's of more than 290 million stg.
The CTW deal follows ALIT's acquisition on February 11 of Minories Underwriting Agencies Limited.
With CTW ALIT will next year control around 700 million stg of Lloyd's market capacity, which is 10.3 billion stg this year.

ALIT is a corporate spread vehicle which invests in a range of Lloyd's insurance syndicates unlike the dedicated corporate vehicles which funnel all their capital into one or a very small number of syndicates.
"The establishment of ALIS reflects ALIT's long term corporate strategy to develop ALIT as a vehicle for the external investor at Lloyd's," ALIT said.
CTW director David Coulthard was today granted leave in the High Court to remain a director of the company for 12 months, the company said in a statement.
Coulthard and fellow director Hugh Shuttleworth were disqualified as company directors for four and five years respectively on February 4 in an action brought by the Department of Trade and Industry.
A spokesman for CTW said Coulthard will oversee the transfer of its Names to ALIS.
CTW, which has 25 employees, will become a shell company from 1998, but will remain in existence until the accounts of all Names have been closed.
